name: NY-07
label: Safe D

key_factors: District's strong Democratic lean of D+25
Claire Valdez's large fundraising and outside-spending advantage
Open seat after Velázquez's retirement, adding some uncertainty
model.rationale: The district's D+25 partisan lean and the fundamentals point to a comfortable Democratic hold, and Polymarket prices the Democratic candidate near certain to win. Valdez has raised over $1.6 million with outside support while the Republican has reported no fundraising, so the forecast stays near the baseline at roughly D+26.
model.watch: An open seat with no polling means a surprise primary fallout or late outside spending could narrow the margin, though a Republican win remains very unlikely.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.
Open seat: Nydia Velázquez (D) is not on the ballot.

overview:
Nydia Velázquez's retirement leaves this heavily Democratic Brooklyn-Queens seat open, but the district's D+25 partisan lean makes it a very difficult target for Republicans. Claire Valdez has built a strong financial position, raising about $1.7 million and drawing over $1.2 million in outside support, while Republican Melvin Rivera has reported no fundraising and no outside spending. Prediction markets put the Democratic candidate's win probability around 97 percent.

With no general-election polls and no expert ratings, the forecast rests on fundamentals and money, which both point the same way. The main source of uncertainty is the open-seat dynamic rather than any sign of a competitive race.
